resources.string: Run a restaurant. Try not to burn it down.
Your restaurant and everything in it will be gone for good.
Anything with a red ! needs you. Tap it to sort it out.
Open the doors and serve. Tap where the green ring points: it shows you each step as it comes up. New things arrive as the days go by, and you\'ll be told before they do.
See how you did, then on to the next day.
Keep your money above zero and your guests happy. How many days can you last?
New dish unlocked: %1$s. Tap the menu sign to add it.
The pantry is empty! Tap the pantry and buy food before you open.
%1$s is about to collapse! Tap them and give them a day off.
%1$s is about to collapse! Hire a second cook, then give them a day off.
%1$s is worn out. Tap them and give them a day off.
Tap anything with a red ! to sort it out
Table %1$d wants to order. Tap the table.
Table %1$d would like drinks. Tap the table.
Tap the bar to pour the drinks.
Table %1$d\'s drinks are on the bar. Tap the tray to pick them up.
Take the drinks to table %1$d. Tap the table.
Table %1$d is having a drink and reading the menu…
Take the order to the chef. Tap the chef.
Table %1$d\'s food is ready. Tap the plate.
Take the food to table %1$d. Tap the table.
Guests are waiting at the door! Clear table %1$d so they can sit.
Table %1$d needs clearing. Tap it to pick up the dirty plates.
Take the dirty plates to the dish station (top right).
Someone spilled! Tap the mop bucket, then tap the spill.
Tap the spill to mop it up.
Floor\'s clean. Tap the bucket to put the mop back.
The kitchen is out of food, so guests are leaving. Restock in the morning.
Everyone\'s gone. Clearing up, then it\'s closing time.
Last job: clear table %1$d, then wash up to close.
The fridge broke! Nobody can order until it\'s fixed. Tap the fridge.
The fridge is struggling! It\'s about to give up.
Fridge: fix it if it breaks
A food critic just walked in! Only you can serve them: be quick and good.
A celebrity just walked in! Only you can serve them. Keep them happy.
A health inspector just walked in! Only you can serve them. Keep it clean.
The food critic loved it! Your stars went up.
The food critic was not impressed. Your stars went down.
The celebrity had a great time. Expect a crowd tomorrow!
The celebrity left unhappy, and told everyone.
You failed the health inspection: a 60 coin fine.
A rat! Tap it to chase it out before the guests notice.
Pan fire! Nothing cooks until you put it out. Tap the stove.
A dog sneaked in and is begging! Tap it to lead it out.
Power cut! The kitchen\'s stopped. Tap the fuse box by the door.
Trouble: tap to sort it out
A new hire tripped and dropped their tray! Clean up the mess.
The cat knocked table %1$d\'s food off! The chef is making it again.
Waiting for guests to come in…
The chef is cooking table %1$d\'s order…
Your guests are eating. Enjoy the quiet!
Food for table %1$d: pick it up
Drinks for table %1$d. Tap to pick them up.
having a drink and reading the menu
Mop bucket: pick up or put back the mop
Spill on the floor: mop it up
You. Tap to undo your last stop.
That\'s all %1$d stops lined up. Finish one, or tap yourself to undo the last.
You need another cook. Your kitchen can cook about %1$s, but %2$s.
You need another server. There are too many guests for your floor staff to look after.
You need a bartender. The bar is open and the room is too busy for you to pour every drink yourself.
You need a dishwasher. The place is getting dirty and nobody\'s clearing up.
Staff drop trays now and then. New staff do it most in their first %1$d shifts, and tired or unreliable ones keep doing it. Someone has to mop up after them.
You have enough staff for now. Everyone you hire adds to your daily costs.
Every night makes a mess. A dishwasher keeps up with it. Let it get too dirty and the rats move in.
%1$d gave up waiting for a table
%1$d left with no table free. Clear tables as soon as guests leave.
%1$d left before you took their order. Get to tables with a ? sooner.
%1$d left waiting for food. Pick plates up from the counter quickly.
%1$d left waiting for drinks. Take drinks orders, then tap the bar to pour them.
%1$d left with no table free, and nobody was clearing for you. Hire a dishwasher.
%1$d left waiting for drinks. You had no bartender, so every drink was yours to pour. Hire one.
%1$d left waiting for food. You had no server to carry plates out. Hire one.
%1$d went hungry because food ran out. Restock the pantry.
%1$d found nothing on the menu for them. Try cheaper or different dishes.
%1$d went hungry because the kitchen couldn\'t keep up. Hire a cook.
You reached this week\'s goal! Reward: %1$s
Decorations are yours for good, and every guest enjoys their evening a little more for them.
Hosts and bussers apply once you have %1$s.
Nobody\'s looking for work right now. Check back in a few days.
Tops up everything to two nights\' worth: %1$s.
They leave for good, and it costs %1$s.
They\'re your only cook: without them nobody cooks tonight, and every order takes ages.
Ingredients %1$s a plate, so you keep %2$s
Nothing on tonight\'s menu for guests who are %1$s. They\'ll walk out.
Tables: see how many you have, or buy more
A new table arrives free each morning until you have %1$d.
Another table means more guests every night, and more to run around for.
Table %1$d is going in this morning.
The room is full. That\'s as many tables as it can hold.
Broken. The kitchen works at half speed.
Looking after it costs less than fixing it once it breaks.
Broken! Cold food spoils fast and dishes that need it can\'t be made.
Worn out. It could break down, even during service.
A %1$s breaks down less and wears out more slowly.
This is the best fridge money can buy.
A %1$s cooks faster, breaks down less and wears out more slowly.
A new %1$s is going in this morning.
This is the best oven money can buy.
The restaurant ran out of money.
Nobody wants to eat here anymore.

Your reputation is %1$d out of 100. More stars bring more guests every night.

Stars go up when guests leave happy: good food, fair prices and quick service.

They go down when guests wait too long, go hungry, or the place is dirty. Bad reviews and inspections can knock them down too.
Paid whether or not anyone comes in. Food is extra, when you buy it.
Cooks the food. More cooks means more dishes at once.
Carries food and drinks out to the tables. Doesn\'t clear them: that\'s a dishwasher\'s job.
Clears tables and washes up. Doesn\'t mop or fix anything: that\'s you.
Helps carry food and drinks out to the tables, like a server.
Greets guests at the door: they wait longer, and one more party fits inside.
Clears tables and washes up, so you don\'t have to.
Takes drink orders at the tables and pours them at the bar. A server (or you) has to carry each numbered tray to its table.
Your game is saved. Tap Continue on the start screen to carry on.
Tonight is saved right where you are. Tap Continue on the start screen to carry on.
Your game is saved, but this morning\'s changes (buying, hiring and so on) won\'t be kept.
Nothing yet. New things arrive as the days go by.
Switch on every new thing and every dish now, instead of one at a time. Only in the morning.
Someone\'s spilt something, and guests hate a dirty floor. Tap the mop bucket by the door, then tap the spill to mop it up.

Guests now like a drink before they eat. Tap a table with a glass bubble to take the order, tap the bar to pour it, then carry the drinks over. A bartender takes the orders and pours, but a server or you must carry each numbered tray to its table.
A cat has moved in. Guests love it when it sits by their table, but don\'t leave plates on the counter: it knocks them off.
Grown-ups with children are coming in. Children drop their food, so expect a mess to mop when they leave.
Someone famous just walked in. Only you can serve them, so staff leave their table alone. Look after them and word gets around: more guests tomorrow.
A critic is here to review you. Only you can serve them, so staff leave their table alone. Good food served quickly means a glowing review and more stars.
A rat is scurrying about and putting guests off their food. Tap it to chase it out.
Now and then a guest asks for something: the wrong dish, cold food, or the bill. Staff can\'t help with this. Tap their table to sort it out, or it costs you.
A bad night for the staff!
Someone has gone home sick, walked out after a row, or taken a long break. The others carry on, but you\'ll have to cover for the one who\'s gone.
An old fridge can give up mid-service. While it\'s broken nobody can order cold food: tap the fridge to fix it.
A dog has sneaked in and is begging at the tables. Tap it to lead it out.
Your cooks\' moods now show in their cooking. A grumpy cook burns food; a happy one makes chef\'s specials. Days off and good nights keep them cheerful.
A pan has caught fire and nothing can cook. Tap the stove to put it out.
An inspector is checking the place. Only you can serve them, so staff leave their table alone. Keep the floor clean and the tables cleared, or you\'ll be fined.
The lights are out and the kitchen has stopped. Tap the fuse box by the door to get them back on.
Some nights, a second thing goes wrong once the first is sorted. Stay sharp!
A quieter night tonight. Catch your breath!
guests start asking for things only you can fix. Watch the tables!
your staff will have bad nights. Be ready to cover for them.
guests start spilling things. Grab the mop!
guests will want a drink first. Pour them at the bar!
a cat might wander in. Guests love a visit!
families with children come in, and children drop food!
a food critic might come to review you!
watch out for rats! Tap one to chase it out.
an old fridge can break mid-service. Tap it to fix it.
a dog might sneak in. Tap it to lead it out.
your cooks\' moods start to show in their cooking.
pans can catch fire! Tap the stove to put it out.
the health inspector might visit. Keep the floor clean!
the power can cut out. Tap the fuse box by the door.
some nights, two things will go wrong.
A big menu: %1$d%% more guests come tonight.
A small menu: %1$d%% fewer guests come tonight. Serve more dishes to draw more people.
More dishes on the menu bring more guests.
Takes a while to cook, but most guests are happy with it.
Cooks at an ordinary pace. Cheap, and free of every allergen.
The quickest dish to make: handy on a busy night.
Quick to cook and cheap. Children love them.
Quick to cook, but eggs go off fast: keep them stocked.
Slow to cook, and a grumpy cook burns it easily. The celebrity\'s favourite.
Pricey and slow. The critic\'s favourite, but it\'s gone by morning if the fridge breaks.

plurals.name: chefs_specials
plurals.item: The chef was in a great mood: one table got a chef\'s special!
The chef was in a great mood: %d tables got a chef\'s special!

plurals.name: chef_burnt
plurals.item: The chef was grumpy and burnt one order. Cheer the cooks up with a day off.
The chef was grumpy and burnt %d orders. Cheer the cooks up with a day off.
